questions.q: How should you answer 'what's architecturally different between Oracle's instance and database compared to SQL Server'?
options: Explain that in Oracle the instance (SGA plus background processes) and the database (physical datafiles) are conceptually separate things, unlike how SQL Server draws that line
Say Oracle and SQL Server use identical terminology, just different keywords
Say the instance and database are always on different physical servers
Avoid the question since Oracle's architecture wasn't covered in this course
questions.explain: The lesson explains that Oracle's instance/database separation is a real conceptual distinction, referencing the FINPRD setup from Lesson 92.

questions.q: What framework does this lesson recommend for answering 'how would you migrate a SQL Server database to PostgreSQL'?
options: Assess the project's scope first, then work through key platform differences, then pick ETL tooling — not naming tools first
Immediately recommend a specific third-party migration tool without further discussion
Explain that such a migration is never possible
Describe only the CREATE TABLE syntax differences
questions.explain: The lesson recommends Chapter 17's assessment-first sequence — scope, then differences, then tooling — as it demonstrates judgment rather than memorization.

questions.q: What made the Lesson 94 Oracle tuning story an effective example interview answer, per this lesson?
options: It was specific and included a concrete before-and-after result (20 minutes down to under a minute)
It avoided naming any specific tools or commands
It described a purely hypothetical scenario with no numbers
It focused only on abstract database theory
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that a strong interview answer is specific and quantifies the before/after result, exactly like the Oracle AWR/index/statistics fix.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a candidate should do if asked directly whether Harborline Retail Group is a real employer?
options: Be honest that it's a hands-on lab project built while learning, not a claimed employer, since the technical reasoning behind it is what matters
Claim it was a real past employer to sound more credible
Refuse to discuss the project at all
Avoid the topic by changing the subject
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly advises honesty about the project being a learning exercise, while noting the technical content itself is real and defensible.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the single hardest part of migrating SQL Server logic to Oracle?
options: Procedural code — T-SQL's TRY...CATCH and control-flow syntax don't map one-to-one onto PL/SQL, so stored procedures and triggers usually need rewriting
Choosing a font for SQL*Plus
Renaming tables to match Oracle naming conventions
There is no meaningful difference between T-SQL and PL/SQL
questions.explain: The lesson points to procedural code differences as the hardest part, consistent with Chapter 17 Lesson 86's coverage of SQL Server-to-Oracle migration.
